For $r\ge0$ let $T_r=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_rangle$ be the ring of restricted series [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. For $f=\sum_{

source.place: Section 1.2, Corollary 4, printed p.10 (PDF p.11): arbitrary-series unit criterion following Gauss multiplicativity and completeness. Read primary PDF online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], the Gauss norm is a complete nonarchimedean submultiplicative ring norm. A nonzero restricted family attains its norm: choose a coefficient of size $b>0$; the finite nonempty set of coefficients of size $\ge b/2$ has maximum $M\ge b$, and all remaining coefficients have size $<b/2<M$. Thus $M$ is the global maximum. The same argument applies after deleting the constant coefficient. Coefficientwise scalar multiplication gives $\|af\|_G=|a|\|f\|_G$ for $a\in K$ (including $a=0$).

source.place: Section 1.2, Gauss norm defined by the coefficient maximum, printed pp.8-9 Primary PDF read online by Q02 on 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Suppose $fg=1$. Then $f\ne0$. Choose $a\in K^\times$ equal to a coefficient attaining $\|f\|_G$ by step 1, and put $F=a^{-1}f$, $G=ag$. By [lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative], $1=\|f\|_G\|g\|_G$, so $FG=1$ and $\|F\|_G=\|G\|_G=1$. Both belong to the subring $U_r$ of [lem-trf-tate-unit-ball-polynomial-reduction]. Reduction therefore gives $\operatorname{red}(F)\operatorname{red}(G)=1$ in $k[X_1,\ldots,X_r]$, where $k$ is the field supplied by that node. Apply [lem-trf-mvpolynomial-divisor-nonzero-constant] over $k$ with constant $1$: $\operatorname{red}(F)$ is a constant polynomial. It is nonzero since it has inverse $\operatorname{red}(G)$.

The restricted tail $F-F(0)$ has norm $<1$: if nonzero, its norm is attained at a nonconstant coefficient by step 1, and if zero its norm is $0$. Scaling by $a$ gives $\|f-c_0\|_G<|a|=|c_0|$, the required strict supremum inequality.

source.place: Corollary 4, nonzero constant reduction gives strict coefficient dominance, printed p.10 Primary PDF read online by Q02 on 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $\|f-c_0\|_G<|c_0|$. Nonnegativity gives $c_0\ne0$. Set $h=1-c_0^{-1}f=-c_0^{-1}(f-c_0)$. Step 1 gives $\|h\|_G=\|f-c_0\|_G/|c_0|<1$. Completeness from [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] verifies the hypothesis of [lem-trf-complete-normed-ring-geometric-inverse], which supplies $S=\sum_{n\ge0}h^n\in T_r$ with $(1-h)S=S(1-h)=1$. Hence $g=c_0^{-1}S$ satisfies $fg=1$. For $r=0$ there is only the constant coefficient, the tail norm is $0$, and both directions reduce to invertibility of a nonzero element of $K$; $f=0$ satisfies neither condition.
